item.title: Strangeness-to-entropy ratio across the QCD crossover
item.description:
Authors: Artemiy Lysenko, Mark I. Gorenstein, Marek Gazdzicki, Roman Poberezhniuk, Volodymyr Vovchenko

Updated: 2026-11-17

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We study the absolute open-strangeness density $n_{|S|}$ of strongly interacting matter at vanishing conserved-charge chemical potentials. Unlike the net-strangeness susceptibility $χ_2^S$, this quantity is not a derivative of the QCD partition function and requires a microscopic specification of the strangeness carriers. We use an equation of state that interpolates between an interacting hadron resonance gas and a quark-gluon plasma, with parameters fixed previously by lattice-QCD bulk thermodynamics. The ratio of $n_{|S|}$ to the entropy density $s$ follows the hadron-gas behavior below $T\simeq120$ MeV, rises above the ideal massless $2+1$-flavor limit of approximately $0.053$ across the crossover, and approaches this limit from above at high temperature. The same equation of state, minimally extended to finite $μ_S$, captures the temperature dependence of the lattice-QCD $χ_2^S$. For uncorrelated singly-strange Boltzmann particles, the strangeness fluctuation factor $F_S=χ_2^S/(n_{|S|}/T^3)$ equals unity. Within the constructed equation of state, it deviates from unity by less than $10\%$. This allows us to estimate $n_{|S|}/s$ from lattice-QCD data on $χ_2^S$ and $s$. The lattice-based estimate reaches a maximum of $n_{|S|}/s\simeq0.063$ at $T\simeq220$ MeV, followed by a $20\%$ decrease towards the high-temperature limit.

item.title: Strange-Metal Magnetotransport without a Strange-Metal Ground State
item.description:
Authors: Yongjun Ahn, Matteo Baggioli, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Keun-Young Kim

Updated: 2026-11-17

Category: hep-th

Abstract:

Strange metals display a linear-in-temperature resistivity, $ρ_{xx}\sim T$, and a quadratic inverse Hall angle, $\cotΘ_H\sim T^2$. These seemingly universal laws are often attributed to quantum criticality, yet no controlled theory realizes both at an asymptotic zero-temperature fixed point, and experimentally they persist only over finite temperature windows. Here, we show that these properties can arise from an intermediate critical regime that does not govern the ground state. Using a minimal class of holographic models, we construct a fully backreacted realization of both scalings, which appear within a finite temperature window controlled by an emergent intermediate scaling geometry. The window is bounded by relevant deformations of the corresponding fixed point: momentum relaxation sets the upper edge, while the magnetic field $B$ closes it from below at $T_{\min}\sim B^{2/3}$, up to logarithmic corrections. At $T_{\min}$, strange-metal transport, the scaling geometry, and critical thermodynamics break down together. Our results point to intermediate criticality as a distinct route to strange-metal transport, and suggest that it can be identified by the simultaneous breakdown of transport and thermodynamic scaling under a magnetic field.

item.title: Observation of Strong Directed Flow for $φ$ Mesons in the High Baryon Density Region at RHIC
item.description:
Authors: Guangyu Zheng

Updated: 2026-11-17

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

We report measurements of the rapidity-odd directed flow ($v_{1}$) of $φ$ mesons in 10--40\% Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{sNN}=3.0$--4.5 GeV from the STAR fixed-target program at RHIC, together with the collider-energy measurement at $\sqrt{sNN}=7.7$ GeV. Despite its mesonic nature, the $φ$-meson $v_{1}$ exhibits a magnitude comparable to that of protons and $Λ$ baryons and is significantly larger than that of $K^{0}_{S}$ mesons in the high-baryon-density region. Comparisons with UrQMD calculations indicate that the observed $φ$-meson directed flow is consistent with production through high-mass baryon resonances and the collective motion of baryons influenced by baryonic mean-field interactions. These results provide new experimental constraints on baryon-resonance production and strange-hadron transport dynamics in dense QCD matter.

item.title: Covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus, non-dissipative transport and the chiral anomaly in inhomogeneous systems with nontrivial momentum-space topology
item.description:
Authors: M. A. Zubkov

Category: hep-th

Abstract:

We review, systematize and extend the covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus for fermions in non-Abelian gauge fields and its applications to systems inhomogeneous in coordinate space with nontrivial momentum-space topology: the non-Abelian chiral separation and quantum Hall effects, their stability under interactions, the Fermi-surface invariant of inhomogeneous systems and the non-elliptic models that carry it, the factorization of the chiral anomaly into the instanton number and the momentum-space invariant $N_3$, and the noncommutative-geometric form of the invariants.

item.title: Open Heavy Flavor in Nuclear Collisions: From Lattice QCD to Observables
item.description:
Authors: Yu Fu, Steffen A. Bass, Tharun Krishna, Ralf Rapp, Weiyao Ke

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Heavy quarks serve as excellent probes of the Quark-Gluon-Plasma (QGP) produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Here, we report on a comprehensive framework that transports charm quarks from their initial production through the QGP medium, hadronization, and the hadronic phase to final observables in experiments. For the transport through the QGP fireball, which is described by 2+1D relativistic viscous fluid dynamics, we employ an extended Langevin equation that combines elastic diffusion processes with medium-induced radiation, including interference effects. The charm-quark transport coefficients are derived from nonperturbative $T$-matrix interactions, which are constrained by lattice QCD and also produce an equation of state for the thermal medium which is consistent with the one employed in the hydrodynamic simulations. Pre-hadronic resonant states which emerge in the $T$-matrix near the QGP transition temperature naturally lead to a transition to hadronic degrees of freedom. This transition is realized in two different approaches: a coalescence model augmented with 4-momentum conservation and the resonance recombination model, both supplemented with fragmentation functions constrained by charm-hadron spectra in proton-proton collisions at the LHC and RHIC. The late-stage rescattering of charm hadrons is assessed with schematic heavy-light cross sections implemented into a hadronic transport model. We report results for the nuclear modification factors and elliptic flows of $D^0$ and $D_s^+$ mesons and $Λ_c^+$ baryons, together with the $D_s^+/D^0$ and $Λ_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios. The calculations are compared with measurements from the ALICE and CMS collaborations in Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\NN}}=5$\,TeV and with STAR data in Au-Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\NN}}=200$\,GeV.

item.title: Unraveling QCD dynamics via charm-tagged jets with ALICE at the LHC
item.description:
Authors: Emma Yeats

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: hep-ex

Abstract:

The study of jet substructure provides tests of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and offers differential ways to study hadronization mechanisms. QCD predicts that jet radiation patterns depend on the mass and color charge of the initiating parton. Parton showers are sensitive to the different Casimir factors of quarks and gluons, and to the parton mass through the dead-cone effect. In this talk, we present three sets of $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jet measurements. First, we present the first measurement of the Energy-Energy Correlator (EEC) for $\textrm{D}^0$-meson-tagged jets. This observable reveals the detailed structure of QCD radiation from heavy quarks, allowing for a distinction between perturbative and non-perturbative effects in charm-quark showers. We then discuss measurements of the angular differences between three different axis definitions inside the jets. The three definitions offer different sensitivity to wide-angle soft radiation and systematically probe the radiation pattern from charm quarks. The final measurement regards jet angularities, which characterize the weighted angular distribution of the jet constituents. These powerful observables probe the parton shower, with sensitivity to parton-mass and Casimir-factor related effects that can be tuned by adjusting the importance of wide-angle radiation.

item.title: Inclusive Heavy Quarkonium Production in Lepton-Hadron Scattering in a Joint QCD+QED Factorization Approach
item.description:
Authors: Jian-Wei Qiu, Kazuhiro Watanabe, Jia-Yue Zhang

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will provide an opportunity for precision studies of heavy quarkonium production in electron-proton ($ep$) and electron-nucleus ($eA$) collisions. Comparing production in $ep$ and $eA$ collisions provides a clean, well-controlled experimental environment to study interactions between a heavy quark pair and nuclear matter and the formation of quarkonia in a nuclear medium. In this talk, we present the first calculation of heavy quarkonium production in both $ep$ and $eA$ collisions at EIC energies using a joint QCD+QED factorization framework that treats collision-induced QCD and QED radiation on equal footing, and discuss the role of the nuclear medium in exploring how a physical quarkonium is emerged from a produced heavy quark pair. We also systematically extend our calculation to include next-to-leading power contributions in the inverse power expansion of quarkonium transverse momentum, and discuss the matching of our calculations to fixed-order calculations in the nonrelativistic Quantum Chromodynamics (NRQCD) approach.

item.title: Third-body-corrected Two-Pion Femtoscopic Correlations in Au+Au Collisions at High Baryon Density
item.description:
Authors: Youquan Qi

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Identical charged pion femtoscopy provides a sensitive probe of the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions. At high baryon density, the differences between $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ Hanbury Brown--Twiss (HBT) radii may originate from both the third-body Coulomb effect and the initial-state isospin asymmetry. Since the latter is related to the equation of state (EoS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, separating these two effects is essential. In these proceedings, we present the measurements of identical charged pion correlations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=3.0$, 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, 4.5, and 7.7 GeV collected by the STAR experiment. A correction procedure is developed to remove the residual third-body Coulomb effect. After correction, the extracted HBT radii of $π^+π^+$ and $π^-π^-$ become consistent within uncertainties. The results indicate that the observed charge dependence is dominated by the third-body Coulomb effect, while any remaining contribution from the initial-state isospin asymmetry to the relative HBT radius difference, $(R_{π^-}-R_{π^+})/R_{π^+}$, is constrained to be less than 5\% at the 95\% confidence level.

item.title: Heavy-quark gluon radiation in transversely flowing QCD matter: First-subeikonal corrections
item.description:
Authors: Bojana Ilic, Magdalena Djordjevic

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We investigate medium-induced gluon radiation from energetic heavy quarks propagating through a finite-size QCD medium with transverse collective flow. Within the DGLV framework, we calculate the radiation spectrum at first order in opacity and to first-subeikonal accuracy, retaining finite heavy-quark and effective gluon masses. Subleading corrections to the longitudinal propagator poles generate mass-dependent modifications of both the residue denominators and formation phases. For rotationally symmetric transverse-momentum integration domains, all contributions linear in the transverse flow velocity vanish after full azimuthal integration, while a nonzero static first-subeikonal correction remains. For representative medium parameters, this correction increases the integrated fractional radiative energy loss by approximately $10$--$20\%$, depending on the quark mass, initial energy, and path length. At the differential level, transverse flow produces a dipolar angular anisotropy, enhancing radiation along the flow direction and suppressing it in the opposite direction.

item.title: Suppression, flow, and chemical components of heavy flavor hadrons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions within an improved Langevin framework
item.description:
Authors: Shu-Qing Li, Wen-Jing Xing, Shanshan Cao, Guang-You Qin

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We improve the Langevin model to incorporate both perturbative and non-perturbative interactions between heavy quarks and the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The transport coefficient of heavy quarks is evaluated by a potential scattering model in which both the short-range Yukawa interaction and the long-range string interaction are included. The updated model provides the correct thermal equilibrium limit of the heavy quark system with the medium background, and improves the accuracy in describing the nuclear modification factor and elliptic flow coefficient of $D$ mesons observed at RHIC and the LHC. Nuclear modification of different chemical components of charm hadrons, including $D^0$, $D_s^+$, $Λ_c^+$, $Ξ_c^0$, and $Ω_c^0$, is investigated. Their spectrum ratios are found sensitive to not only the hadronization mechanism of charm quarks but also the medium-modified charm quark spectrum in heavy-ion collisions, offering additional constraints on the heavy quark dynamics inside a color-deconfined nuclear medium.

item.title: Reduced Density Matrices from Renormalization-Group Flows
item.description:
Authors: X. Zhen, Z. Y. Meng, J. C. Pei, F. R. Xu

Updated: 2026-11-16

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We reconstruct complete one- and two-body reduced density matrices (RDMs) by a single collective backward evolution along the in-medium similarity renormalization-group flow. Benchmarks show improved accuracy and physical consistency over conventional elementwise evolution. In neutron matter, two-body RDMs reveal spin-triplet dominance in interaction-dependent Fermi-sea depletion trends. Meanwhile, the forward-backward energy difference provides an internal diagnostic of many-body truncation errors, whose quantification remains challenging in nuclear $ab\ initio$ calculations.

item.title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
item.description:
Authors: Fengxi Yan, Ting Liu, Rongrong Ma, Yunshuang Qin, Shule Wu, Shenghui Zhang, Fan Si

Updated: 2026-11-15

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($ΔN_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

item.title: Nuclear Mott transition with neural quantum states
item.description:
Authors: Zi-Xiao Zhang, Xiao-Lu Qian, Wan-Bing He, Gerd Röpke, Kai-Jia Sun, Yu-Gang Ma

Updated: 2026-11-15

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Bound clusters can dissolve in nuclear matter due to Pauli blocking, a phenomenon known as the Mott transition that is a key determinant of the nuclear abundances in heavy-ion collisions. Microscopic descriptions of this behavior require solving the in-medium Schrödinger equation. However, this remains a major computational challenge because the nuclear medium breaks Galilean invariance and couples angular-momentum channels at finite center-of-mass momentum. The emergence of weakly bound states near dissociation further places stringent demands on conventional methods. Here, we address these challenges by introducing MottNet, a momentum-space neural quantum state framework based on self-attention that directly solves the $A$-body in-medium Schrödinger equation. Benchmarked against exact diagonalization of the in-medium deuteron, MottNet reveals substantially weaker Mott suppression for $α$ particles in hot and dense nuclear matter than do conventional calculations based on combined approximations. At high baryon densities, the predicted $α$-particle abundance is enhanced by orders of magnitude, even after continuum-edge subtraction. This finding offers a microscopic explanation for the unexpectedly large $α$-particle fraction inferred from a combined analysis of FOPI heavy-ion collision data and transport model calculations.

item.title: A Differentiable Surrogate for Loss-Dominated Ion Beam Transport
item.description:
Authors: Jose M. Munoz-Arias, Laura Ruiz-Arango, Derick Gonzalez-Acevedo, Fabian C. Pastrana-Cruz, Jackson Hacias, Ronald F. Garcia Ruiz

Updated: 2026-11-15

Category: physics.ins-det

Abstract:

Radioactive nuclei with extreme proton-to-neutron ratios provide unique probes of nuclear structure, fundamental symmetries, astrophysical processes, and applications such as medicine. However, their short half-lives and low production rates mean that experiments must work with few desired ions, often amid contaminant backgrounds exceeding the signal by six orders of magnitude. Efficiently isolating, transporting, and delivering these ions through multi-stage apparatus is therefore a central challenge. We introduce a differentiable probabilistic surrogate for ion-beam transport in regimes dominated by particle loss. The model jointly captures the survival probability of ions along the beamline and the evolving phase-space distribution of the surviving particles by combining discrete-time survival analysis with conditional normalizing flows. Applied to a high-dimensional electrostatic beamline, the resulting likelihood enables gradient-based optimization of operating voltages and inference of beam properties from sparse detector observations. Once trained, the surrogate provides millisecond-scale differentiable predictions, transforming particle-tracking simulations with hard losses into an inference-ready model for experimental design, beamline optimization, and future digital twins of experiments with rare nuclei.

item.title: Fluctuation modes in the initial state of heavy-ion collisions: from 2D to 3D hybrid simulations
item.description:
Authors: Renata Krupczak

Updated: 2026-11-14

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

This dissertation investigates how the initial stages of relativistic heavy-ion collisions shape the evolution of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the observables measured experimentally. Particular attention is given to the initial state and pre-equilibrium dynamics, which constitute the main sources of uncertainty in hybrid simulations. The first part of the dissertation reviews the framework underlying state-of-the-art hybrid simulations and the numerical tools used in phenomenological analyses. The second part studies the matching between pre-equilibrium evolution and viscous hydrodynamics. Since commonly used conformal kinetic-theory descriptions are inconsistent with the non-conformal hydrodynamic equation of state, an entropy-density matching prescription is proposed. This prescription reduces the artificial bulk pressure generated at the switching time and improves the consistency of the hybrid framework. The third part develops a mode-by-mode decomposition of initial energy-density profiles to isolate fluctuation modes and quantify their contributions to final observables. Applied to Pb-Pb collisions across centrality classes and extended to a fully three-dimensional O-O collision system, the method shows that initial fluctuations survive hydrodynamic evolution and leave measurable imprints on final observables. In O-O collisions, fluctuations can dominate over geometric effects from the impact parameter, demonstrating that intermediate-sized systems are not simply scaled-down versions of large systems. Overall, these results provide tools for constraining the early stages of heavy-ion collisions and for understanding how fluctuations propagate through the QGP evolution.

item.title: $α$--$α$ Correlations in Excited Clustering Nuclei Across the Solid-Liquid Transition
item.description:
Authors: Yong-Hao Jin, Xi-Guang Cao, Yu-Gang Ma

Updated: 2026-11-14

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We investigate the structural evolution of $α$-cluster matter using a microscopic transport model for four $α$-conjugate collision systems, including $^{12}\text{C}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}+^{12}\text{C}$, $^{28}\text{Si}+^{12}\text{C}$, and $^{40}\text{Ca}+^{12}\text{C}$ at incident energies ranging from 2.0 to 7.0~MeV/u. The $α$-cluster structure of an excited nucleus undergoes a solid-liquid phase transition with increasing incident energy. Whether it proceeds by the dissociation of individual clusters or by the collapse of their spatial organization remains unexplored, as does the question of whether any characteristic $α$--$α$ correlation survives. The one-body density $ρ(\mathbf{r})$, the standard clustering diagnostic, cannot by itself settle this question, since it neither distinguishes a genuine cluster configuration from a density fluctuation nor reveals the sparse residual clusters masked by the surrounding nucleon medium. We therefore construct the exclusive $α$--$α$ two-body spatial correlation function from the $α$-cluster centroids to isolate the $α$ clusters. In all four systems the $α$--$α$ correlation exhibits two peaks, a nearest-neighbor one and a next-nearest-neighbor inter-cluster one. Both peak positions increase with system size. Over the energy range studied, which spans this transition, the mean number of $α$ clusters per event falls steeply while the $α$--$α$ correlation persists and the inter-cluster distances change only slightly. The individual clusters therefore dissociate rather than lose their spatial organization.

item.title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$μ$C: Nucleus Options
item.description:
Authors: Ali Can Canbay, Burak Dagli, Arda Goroglu, Yigitali Karaca, Umit Kaya, Bora Ketenoglu, Saleh Sultansoy, Frank Zimmermann

Updated: 2026-11-13

Category: hep-ex

Abstract:

Nucleus options of the LH$μ$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $μ^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $μ$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $μ$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $μ$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $μ$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

item.title: Novel observables for exploring jet quenching effects in individual jets
item.description:
Authors: Jin-Wen Kang, Sa Wang, Meng-Quan Yang, Ben-Wei Zhang, Enke Wang

Updated: 2026-11-13

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We introduce event-shape observables in the jet frame to characterize intra-jet shapes and study medium modifications in heavy-ion collisions. Using the JEWEL model, we investigate jet constituent angular and transverse momentum distributions, together with two representative event-shape observables, transverse thrust $τ_\perp$ and transverse sphericity $S_\perp$, in $p$+$p$ and 0--10% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.02\,\mathrm{TeV}$. These observables are evaluated after transforming the jet constituent momenta into the jet frame. The intra-jet shape distributions in Pb+Pb collisions shift toward larger values relative to those in $p$+$p$ collisions, indicating more isotropic distributions of constituent transverse momenta. Comparisons between calculations with and without recoil, along with the dependence on the constituent transverse momentum threshold, indicate that medium response plays an important role in these modifications. These results suggest that jet-frame event-shape observables provide sensitive probes of medium response in jet quenching, complementary to single-particle angular and transverse momentum distributions.

item.title: Searching for signatures of criticality in heavy-ion collisions using two-pion correlation functions
item.description:
Authors: Alejandro Ayala, Santiago Bernal-Langarica, Máté Csanád, Isabel Domínguez, Irving I. Gaspar, Luis A. Hernández, Johannes Jahan, Micheal Kahangirwe, Jamie M. Karthein, Dániel Kincses, Grégoire Pihan, Tomáš Poledníček, María Elena Tejeda-Yeomans, Boris Tomášik

Updated: 2026-11-13

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We study possible signatures of the existence of a Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) critical end-point in low-energy relativistic heavy-ion collisions using two-pion femtoscopy. We simulate central $^{209}\mathrm{Bi}+^{209}\mathrm{Bi}$ collisions at center-of-mass energies ranging from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5.8$ to 11 GeV using the EPOS 4.0.3 framework, incorporating an equation of state that explicitly includes a critical end-point and is compatible with lattice QCD results at small baryon chemical potentials. We analyze the pion pair-distance distribution and the corresponding two-pion correlation function by fitting them with Lévy distributions in configuration and momentum spaces, respectively. We find a weak dependence of the source parameters on the collision energy below $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=9.2$ GeV, followed by a change in trend at higher energies, particularly in the intercept parameter $λ$. This behavior may be associated with a decreasing fraction of pions coming from the core and an increasing contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Within the present analysis, we do not identify an unambiguous signal attributable to the critical end-point. A comparison with simulations employing different equation of state parameters to vary the strength of the critical point, as well as with simulations without a critical end-point, is necessary to establish the sensitivity of these observables to critical phenomena.

item.title: Observation of the $Λ(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
item.description:
Authors: ALICE Collaboration

Updated: 2026-11-12

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

A suppression of the baryonic $Λ(1520)$ resonance yield relative to the $Λ$ ground state by $0.589 \pm 0.015^{\rm stat} \pm 0.086^{\rm syst}$ is observed in central relative to peripheral Pb-Pb collisions, with a significance of $6.8σ$. The $Λ(1520)$ production at midrapidity is measured in six centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions for the first time at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV with ALICE. The $Λ(1520)$ is a sensitive probe of late-stage hadronic interactions since its lifetime is comparable to that of the hadronic phase in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC. Statistical hadronization model calculations, predicting yields at chemical freeze-out, overestimate the measured ratio. The transverse-momentum spectra and the centrality dependence of the suppression are reproduced by the MUSIC hydrodynamic model only when coupled to the SMASH hadronic transport afterburner, which implements rescattering and regeneration in the late hadronic stage. The measurement, which represents the first observation of resonance suppression within a single collision system, provides a stringent test of the late-stage dynamics and evidence that hadronic interactions substantially modify reconstructible resonance yield.

item.description:
Authors: Ashish Pandav, Zhangbu Xu, Bedangadas Mohanty

Updated: 2026-11-12

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.

item.title: Holographic viscous transport in scalar-coupled Gauss-Bonnet gravity
item.description:
Authors: Tao Ma, Song He, Li Li

Updated: 2026-11-12

Category: hep-th

Abstract:

item.title: Accelerating exact solutions of relativistic hydrodynamics and Levy-shaped freeze-out sources

item.title: Quantum Correlations Between Two Giant Dipole Resonances in Ultra-Peripheral Collisions
item.description:

Abstract:

item.title: Heavy quarkonium dynamics beyond the binding energy over temperature expansion
item.description:
Authors: Nora Brambilla, Arthur Yi-Ting Lin, Tom Magorsch, Antonio Vairo

Updated: 2026-10-30

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

The equation does not rely on an expansion in the ratio of the binding energy over the temperature, while retaining the Born, Markov, and dilute approximations. It depends on suitable convolutions of Coulombic Green's functions with real-time chromoelectric correlators, rather than a finite set of transport coefficients. It contains jump-operator contributions that enter with both positive and negative signs, so it is not of a Lindblad type. We utilize optimal operator rotations to minimize the negative sector and define a positive-sector approximation that retains only the optimized positive terms, obtaining in this way a Lindblad equation that can be simulated efficiently with the open-source code QTraj for arbitrary chromoelectric spectral functions. We treat the discarded sector as a systematic uncertainty associated with positivity-breaking effects of the pseudo-Lindblad generator. Positivity breaking effects can be attributed to the approximations made in the derivation of the quarkonium master equation, such as the Born--Markov approximations. Using a spectral model constrained by known infrared and ultraviolet limits, we compute the in-medium width and Bjorken-evolved survival probabilities of the $Υ(1\mathrm{S},2\mathrm{S},3\mathrm{S})$. The computations show the convergence of the binding-energy-over-temperature expansion at high temperatures and provide the first large-scale quantum-trajectory simulation results for bottomonium in the low temperature regime. item.title: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions
item.description:
Authors: Jean-François Paquet, Mayank Singh, Derek Teaney

Updated: 2026-10-29

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

We present a numerical study of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for boost-invariant flows in 2+1 dimensions. The Density Frame is a formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is first order in time, requires no auxiliary fields, and has no non-hydrodynamic modes; the only parameters are the shear and bulk viscosities and the equation of state. We formulate the numerical method in terms of a discrete analog of the dissipative function, which guarantees that the discrete equations produce entropy on all length scales and leads to a remarkably robust algorithm. We test the method against the exact solution of kinetic theory in the relaxation time approximation with Gubser symmetry. In making this comparison, we clarify how the kinetic solution matches onto hydrodynamics: we organize the solution by the opacity and show how the Bjorken attractor passes onto the Gubser solution order by order in gradients. We then replace the hydrodynamic engine of the MUSIC code with the Density Frame, and compare the two for IP-Glasma initial conditions in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. The Density Frame smooths sharp gradients more rapidly. The largest differences arise in the bulk-viscous sector, where the bulk pressure in the Density Frame responds instantaneously to the flow, while in the Müller-Israel-Stewart-based MUSIC it relaxes over a finite time. With shear viscosity alone, the multiplicity, mean transverse momentum, and elliptic flow of final-state hadrons from the two codes are very similar. The Density Frame is now ready for a complete Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion data.

item.title: Heavy-Quark Dynamics from $D^{0}$-Meson Anisotropy-Response Scaling Violations
item.description:
Authors: Roy A. Lacey

Updated: 2026-10-21

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

A species-resolved anisotropy-response scaling framework is used to investigate heavy-quark dynamics through the elliptic ($v_2$) and triangular ($v_3$) azimuthal anisotropies of $D^0$ mesons. The independently constrained light-flavor response provides a direct null test: the transformed $D^0$ harmonics exhibit approximate inter-harmonic closure but remain systematically displaced from the kaon-anchored scaling function, revealing a charm scaling violation. The common response is recovered through a charm-specific attenuation rescaling, $k_c$, together with a small low-$p_T$ hadronic-rescattering correction, $ζ_{\rm hs}\simeq0.06$, while retaining the established light-flavor prescription. item.title: Measurements of local polarization of $Λ$ hyperons with event shape engineering in Au+Au collisions at RHIC-STAR
item.description:
Authors: Taiki Kondo

Updated: 2026-10-20

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Anisotropic flow is expected to generate local vorticities along the beam direction, which in turn lead to local polarization of produced particles. Although the local polarization of hyperons has already been observed at RHIC and the LHC, its mechanism is not yet understood: model calculations indicate that the shear-induced and vorticity-induced contributions can have opposite signs and may substantially cancel, so that the resulting polarization depends sensitively on the theoretical implementation. Since both are driven by the anisotropic flow, we employ the Event Shape Engineering (ESE) method, which selects events with different flow magnitudes within a narrow centrality range, to measure the local polarization as a function of the elliptic flow at a fixed multiplicity. We report the measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_2$) and the local polarization ($P_{z,2}$) of $Λ$ and $\barΛ$ as a function of the reduced flow vector magnitude $q_2$ used for the ESE event selection, in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 19.6~{\rm GeV}$ from the STAR experiment. The $v_2$ shows a clear positive dependence on $q_2$, while $P_{z,2}$ indicates a weak positive dependence on $q_2$ and $v_2$. This is the first measurement to directly investigate the relation between anisotropic flow and local polarization, providing new insight into the origin of local polarization.

Abstract:

item.title: Proton-Number Fluctuations in $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U Collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 2.1$ GeV with the CEE Fast Simulation

Authors: Shuaike Lv, Fan Si, Xionghong He, Xu Sun, Yige Huang, Wanbing He, Yifei Zhang, Ming Shao, Ziyang Li

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

A track-by-track efficiency correction method is tested by introducing reconstruction efficiency within the TPC acceptance. The event-sample dependence of the cumulant-ratio uncertainties is further investigated to estimate the statistics required for future measurements, revealing a substantial statistical cost associated with the acceptance compensation. Abstract:

Viscous hydrodynamic simulations demonstrate that the soft EEC of a fluid system is governed by the disconnected contribution, while its elliptic and triangular harmonics respond to the initial geometry and shear viscosity as traditional flow harmonics do. Comparisons between iEBE-VISHNU and PYTHIA for p+p, O+O, and Pb+Pb collisions show that the disconnected contribution dominates at large angles in all systems, whereas connected correlations beyond the mean energy flow grow toward small angles and small systems, most strongly for the harmonics. Abstract:

item.title: Collective-flow signatures of bubble nuclei in intermediate-energy projectile fragmentation reactions
item.description:
Authors: Ge Ren, Chun-Wang Ma, Xi-Guang Cao, Kai-Xuan Cheng, Jie Pu

Updated: 2026-10-14

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Characterized by central density depletion, bubble nuclei represent an important class of exotic nuclear structures. Collective flow in the $^{40}$Ca+$^{9}$Be projectile fragmentation reaction at 140 MeV/u is investigated using the extended quantum molecular dynamics (EQMD) model with a parameter on of the isoscalar monopole excitation strength $\varepsilon$. The projectile $^{40}Ca$ is initialized as a relaxed ten-$α$ cluster configuration exhibiting a bubble-like density distribution. The results reveal that increasing $\varepsilon$ modifies the density distribution and the size of the depleted central region of bubble, producing pronounced changes in fragment yields and collective flow around $\varepsilon\approx0.5$. Below this value, heavy-fragment production plays a significant role, while the directed flow $v_1$ of protons and neutrons remains predominantly negative, indicating preferential emission toward the target side. Above $\varepsilon\approx0.5$, enhanced expansion of the central low-density region suppresses heavy residues and drives $v_1$ toward positive values. In contrast, preformed $α$ clusters show different responses, reflecting their origin in the initial cluster configuration rather than solely in secondary decay. At low excitation, the cluster flow exhibits a pronounced impact-parameter dependence, whereas stronger excitation weakens cluster binding and suppresses directional anisotropy, driving the flow close to zero. The rapidity slopes of the flow coefficients also vary systematically with $\varepsilon$, tracing changes in emission anisotropy during expansion. These findings extend traditional static descriptions by probing the dynamical evolution of exotic structures in heavy-ion reactions and the contrasting collective-flow behavior of preformed clusters and single nucleons constitutes a sensitive dynamical probe of bubble-like structures.

item.title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
item.description:
Authors: Dushmanta Sahu, Kangkan Goswami, Raghunath Sahoo

Updated: 2026-10-12

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. Abstract:

The Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment at the upcoming Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (FAIR) is a high-rate fixed-target experiment designed to investigate nuclear matter at extreme baryon densities in relativistic nucleus-nucleus collisions. To enable high-statistics measurements of rare probes, CBM is designed to operate at event rates up to 10 MHz. This necessitates the development of fast and radiation-tolerant detectors, self-triggered front-end electronics, a free-streaming data acquisition architecture, and real-time event reconstruction capabilities. This dataset enables a detailed evaluation of the operational performance of the detector systems as well as the complete CBM data chain, while the reconstruction of $Λ$ baryons, which constitute a relatively rare signal within the limited geometrical acceptance of mCBM, serves as a natural benchmark. This paper presents the first results on $Λ$ baryon reconstruction with the mCBM experiment, demonstrating the functionality of the detector technologies and the data chain for the upcoming full-scale CBM experiment.

item.title: Deconfinement and the Charge Susceptibility Matrix of QCD
item.description:
Authors: Christopher Grace, Brady Mowbray, Christopher Plumberg

Updated: 2026-10-09

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

At sufficiently high temperatures, lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) calculations predict that nuclear matter undergoes a rapid crossover to a novel, deconfined state known as the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), in which quark flavors essentially behave like independent particles. Here we explore the nature of this transition by introducing two new thermodynamic observables which we refer to as the diagonality and the rescaled curvature of the QCD equation of state (EoS). By comparing these observables in the case of lattice QCD calculations with those of simple toy models and more sophisticated hadronic resonance models, we show that both the diagonality and the rescaled curvature provide complementary insights into the degree of independence between different quark flavors and the underlying degrees of freedom in the system as functions of temperature. We propose that these observables may help to clarify the nature of the transition region and the onset of deconfinement in nuclear matter.

item.description:
Authors: Anibal Bezerra, Fernando G. Gardim

Category: nucl-th

Abstract:

Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.

item.title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
item.description:
Authors: Cong Yi, Xiang-Yu Wu, Zhong Yang, Pi Duan, Guang-You Qin, Xin-Nian Wang, Wenbin Zhao

Updated: 2026-10-09

Category: hep-ph

Abstract:

Energetic partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions induce a medium response that modifies the production of associated hadrons, whose chemical composition provides a sensitive probe of this response. We study jet-associated hadrochemistry using the coupled linear Boltzmann transport and hydrodynamics model with a hybrid hadronization scheme that combines Cooper--Frye particlization, quark coalescence and string fragmentation. For inclusive charged jets in $p+p$ and 0--10\% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$~TeV, the calculated in-cone $K/π$ and $p/π$ ratios are enhanced in Pb+Pb relative to $p+p$ collisions, consistent with preliminary ALICE measurements, with coalescence between shower and thermal partons providing a substantial contribution. After mixed-event acceptance correction and sideband background subtraction, the yields of associated pions, kaons and protons all become negative near $|Δφ|\simeqπ/2$, signaling a depletion caused by the diffusion wake. The $K/π$ and $p/π$ ratios of these deficits remain finite and exceed the $p+p$ values around the jet peaks, indicating that the missing hadrons originate from jet-excited medium. These results establish dijet hadrochemistry as an experimentally accessible tomographic probe of jet-induced medium excitation and the diffusion wake.

item.description:
Authors: Nida Malik

Updated: 2026-10-07

Category: nucl-ex

Abstract:

Investigations involving the event-by-event fluctuations of conserved quantities, like net charge, net baryon number, and strangeness in heavy-ion collisions, provide insights into the properties of quark-gluon plasma (QGP) and the phase diagram of strongly interacting matter. Event-by-event fluctuations of net electric charge in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ and $13.6$ TeV and for OO, Ne-Ne, and Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV are studied by analysing the data collected by the ALICE detector at CERN Large Hadron Collider. The observed dependence of $ν_{\mathrm{dyn}}[+,-]$ on the charged-particle density shows a smooth, energy-independent decrease in the magnitude of $ν_{\mathrm{dyn}}[+,-]$ from smaller to larger collision systems. The negative values of $ν_{\mathrm{dyn}}[+,-]$ indicate a dominance of correlations between oppositely charged particle pairs compared with those arising from like-sign charge pairs. Since $ν_{\mathrm{dyn}}[+,-]$ is known to have an intrinsic dependence on multiplicity, an appropriate scaling is applied. The variable is therefore scaled with the mean multiplicities, $\frac{1}{\frac{1}{\langle N_+ \rangle} + \frac{1}{\langle N_- \rangle}}$. The dependence of the scaled values of $ν_{\mathrm{dyn}}[+,-]$ on charged particle density is also looked into. The results are compared with model calculations from PYTHIA, EPOS4, AMPT and HIJING.
